source_review.native_control: Bsp.cpp startLinkTransport uses Serial1 UART0. SerialUART.cpp begin installs the exclusive UART0_IRQ RX handler; polling is not enabled.
source_review.motor_spi: MotionSetup.cpp configureBus: SPI.setSCK/setTX/setRX, TMC chip select remains SIO.
source_review.torque_spi: BrakeTorqueHw.hpp beginAdc: SPI1 supplied by Bsp.cpp, CONVST/CS remains SIO.
source_review.shared_dacs: Bsp.cpp: Wire.setSDA/setSCL, I2C0 shared by both DAC addresses.
source_review.qs_tx: Bsp.cpp constructs SerialPIO(kFwTrig1, NOPIN). Installed core TX program uses six instructions and one SM; RX-only IRQ path is not active. No PIO block is fixed.
source_review.scope: Reviewed selected production rev2 pin and core-0 resource budget; resource_review records assumptions and exclusions. No whole-program inference.
source_review.analog_monitors: ADC0/ADC2 in PowerSequence, ADC1 in BrakeTorqueHw; ADC3 is reserved angle readback used by SelfTest. This is the pin budget, not a claim that every monitor runs in the delivery loop.
source_review.sdk_default_alarm_pool: SDK pico_time/time.c runtime_init_default_alarm_pool reserves hardware alarm 3 and its TIMER_IRQ_3 through pico_time_adapter. USB and sleep/delay use software slots in that shared owner, not separate hardware alarms.
source_review.arduino_usb: main.cpp __USBStart before setup; RP2040USB.cpp claims one software user IRQ and schedules a default-pool callback. TinyUSB dcd_rp2040.c owns USBCTRL_IRQ via its shared-handler API; modeled as one exclusive aggregate owner, no independent extra clients.
source_review.arduino_cycle_counter: main.cpp rp2040.begin -> RP2040Support.h begin installs SysTick for non-FreeRTOS ARM. No PIO cycle-counter program in this selected path.
source_review.arduino_fifo: main.cpp fifo.begin(1), then registerCore() installs SIO_IRQ_PROC0 even without setup1/loop1; single-core begin does not bypass registerCore.
source_review.application_watchdog: Bsp.cpp enables the watchdog before emitting the boot signature/beacon and keeps it through runtime.
source_review.qp_tick: QF::onStartup -> startTick claims one unused hardware alarm and callback/associated IRQ. It must coexist with SDK alarm 3; its exact number is not fixed by this record.
source_review.dma: Reviewed synchronous SPI transfers, Wire master begin/endTransmission/requestFrom, ADC polling, SerialUART and TX-only SerialPIO. SPI/Wire transferAsync and RP2040 memcpyDMA would introduce DMA demand and need a new review.

assumptions: Selected example examples/PyControlLinkQp, PlatformIO environment mouse_joystick_qp_rev2, generic RP2040, framework-arduinopico 1.40200.0; no extra command-line/environment build overrides.
QS_ON enabled, MJ_BOARD_REV=2; MJ_LINK_USB=0, MJ_SIM_MOTION=0 and MJ_TICK_PROBE=0 defaults from Bsp.cpp. QV on core 0; no setup1/loop1 or FreeRTOS.
Arduino bundled USB path: NO_USB, USE_TINYUSB, DISABLE_USB_SERIAL and DEBUG_RP2040_PORT are not defined. Serial is USB CDC; Serial1 UART0 is configured by the application.
SDK default hardware alarm 3 is enabled. Reviewed installed RP2040 libpico.a disassembly of runtime_init_default_alarm_pool confirms alarm 3 and 16 software timer slots; archive is hashed below.
sdk_startup is the conservative union of SDK/Arduino startup reservations, retained through boot and runtime. Boot pin coverage remains limited to the beacon, not all initialization writes.
No DMA channel claims in the selected synchronous SPI/I2C/ADC, SerialUART RX or transmit-only SerialPIO paths. An empty resources array means none in this reviewed subset, not unused silicon.
Generic variant defines default LED/UART pins, but main/initVariant do not initialize a GPIO LED or default hardware UART in this configuration. USB CDC startup does not claim UART0 GP0/GP1.
excluded: Not whole-program C++/preprocessor/linker inference. New source files, dependencies, build overrides and alternate environments require a fresh review even when the recorded hashes match.

Software timer-slot occupancy (USB plus delay/sleep callers), spinlocks, DMA DREQ/pacing, RAM, clocks, flash/boot ROM, interrupt priorities/latency and multicore vector-table behavior are not budgeted.
No runtime allocator assignment, deployed-image identity, loss/throughput, reset/off-state, electrical or physical debug qualification.
